pr_title: Fix timeline blueprint display not showing correct combo number / colour during placement
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/23533.

| before | after |
| -- | -- |
|![osu Game Tests 2023-05-17 at 08 50 29](https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/191335/5761c55e-131a-4939-b0e8-7df15cc6f872)|![osu Game Tests 2023-05-17 at 08 54 31](https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/191335/d9d198e2-90e6-41d6-a112-c150323a46b7)| 

https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/191335/5b376c4e-ab77-40e3-8f3f-256abb3bfa6e

Of note, in stable the way the editor behaves is slightly differently. The placement object is inserted into the beatmap before being placed, causing future objects to update their combo index, colour, etc.

I'm not ready to commit to that same behaviour (it will probably be a bit more complicated to manage anyway), but will deal with feedback on this in the future.

issue_context.title: The editor timeline always displays to-be-added objects as a new combo
issue_context.body:
Making an issue out of this at least for the parts where the object to be placed uses the first combo colour and a combo index of 1. Dunno what to do about the purple tint applied, that may give off an impression that the object has a different colour. ### Discussed in https://github.com/ppy/osu/discussions/23532
Originally posted by **cihe13375** May 13, 2023 As the title says, no matter if the "new combo" toggle is activated. The display is correct after the object is actually placed down. This is a bit annoying because I am often confused by whether I need to press Q :) ![2023-05-13 22 15 26](https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/33959010/be5bbe24-77b1-473a-87d1-be8926b02b71)

review_comments: Is there a particular reason why this logic is staying local to here, rather than being moved to `UpdateComboInformation()` too? `NewCombo` *is* combo information, after all, and the invariant of "first object always is `NewCombo`" is a nice one to rely on.

It was a bit of a forced hand. By putting it in `UpdateComboInformation` it would get set to `true` on a placement blueprint, which causes it to get stuck in the true state even when it should potentially not be.

I think it makes sense to not be in there because in the 99.99% case, `NewCombo` is externally managed. The "set true for first object" really should only happen at parsing time.

Slightly weird that there's one more linq call here now compared to previous version.

```suggestion
        private HitObject? getPreviousHitObject() => beatmap.HitObjects.LastOrDefault(h => h.StartTime <= startTimeBindable.Value);
```

Also I'm noting the equality change (was `<`, is `<=`) but I'd like to think it shouldn't realistically matter...

The change to `<=` felt more correct. As for why there's more than one linq call: the version I've provided should be faster as it can early abort at the first failure. The original version would iterate over all items.
